question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [EIC's first trading contacts in India and their locations]
options: Surat — Port in Gujarat from which Captain William Hawkins sought Mughal trading permissions in 1608
Agra — Mughal imperial capital where William Hawkins had an audience with Emperor Jahangir (1609–1611)
Calicut — Port on the Malabar Coast where Thomas Best obtained the first Mughal farman for EIC trade in 1612
Swally (Suvali) — Anchorage near Surat where Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese fleet in 1612, enabling EIC trade
wrong_fact: Calicut was NOT where Thomas Best obtained the Mughal farman in 1612. The farman was obtained as a result of Thomas Best's naval victory at the Battle of Swally (near Surat, Gujarat), which impressed the Mughal governor and led to the first English factory being established at Surat — not at Calicut on the Malabar Coast.
explanation: Captain William Hawkins arrived at Surat in 1608 and travelled to Agra, where he met Jahangir (1609–1611). Thomas Best's naval victory at Swally (near Surat) in 1612 over the Portuguese persuaded the Mughals to grant the EIC trading rights. The first factory was established at Surat (Gujarat), not Calicut. Calicut was associated with the Portuguese and the Zamorin's domain.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [EIC's early Indian trading contacts and the ports/courts involved]
options: Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) — Coromandel Coast — EIC established a factory here in 1611, its first on the Indian subcontinent
Hooghly — Bengal — Port from which EIC received first trading rights from the Mughals for Bengal trade
Surat — Gujarat — First major factory granted by Mughal authorities after Battle of Swally (1612)
Ajmer — Rajputana — City where EIC ambassador Thomas Roe presented credentials to Emperor Jahangir (1616)
wrong_fact: Hooghly was NOT the port from which EIC received first Bengal trading rights. The first EIC Bengal factory was established at Hooghly much later (1651). EIC's first Bengal contact was through Masulipatnam and later Balasore; Hooghly became important after 1651 but was NOT the origin of first Mughal-granted Bengal trading rights.
explanation: Masulipatnam (on the Coromandel Coast) was where the EIC established its first Indian factory in 1611. Surat became the main western India factory after 1612. Thomas Roe (not Hawkins) met Jahangir at Ajmer in 1616 and secured a formal treaty. The first Bengal factory was at Hooghly, but not until 1651 — the earlier Mughal permissions for Bengal trade were negotiated through different channels.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Key figures, their missions, and the Indian/Asian locations they operated in]
options: William Hawkins (1608–1611) — Surat and Agra — First English emissary to the Mughal court, spoke Turkish to Jahangir
Nicholas Downton (1614–1615) — Swally anchorage — Defeated the combined Portuguese-Mughal fleet, reinforcing EIC's position at Surat
Thomas Roe (1615–1619) — Ajmer, Mandu, Ahmadabad — First official EIC ambassador to the Mughal court, secured formal trading rights
Paul Canning (1611–1612) — Agra — Succeeded Hawkins as EIC agent at the Mughal court and secured a commercial treaty from Jahangir
wrong_fact: Paul Canning did NOT secure a commercial treaty from Jahangir at Agra. Canning arrived at Agra in 1611 after Hawkins left but failed to obtain any treaty and died in 1611 without achieving his mission. The formal commercial understanding came only after Thomas Best's naval victory (1612) and Thomas Roe's embassy (1615–1619).
explanation: William Hawkins (1608–1611) reached Agra and conversed with Jahangir in Turkish but left without a treaty. Nicholas Downton's 1614–15 naval victories near Swally consolidated the EIC's position. Thomas Roe (official EIC ambassador, 1615–1619) followed the Mughal court to Ajmer, Mandu, and Ahmadabad, and obtained a formal firman for EIC trade. Paul Canning came after Hawkins but died without success — no treaty was secured by him.
